biography: Mary Virginia Allen was born May 4, 1911, in Lafayette County, Florida, the daughter of Lewis Allen and Florence Fryer.

Mary married Frank Mathis (1907–1969) on December 24, 1927, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage was performed by County Judge Moses H. Padgett, following written parental consent because Mary was 15 years old. The couple had two children: Joseph Henry Mathis, born April 19, 1930, and Honorine Virginia Mathis, born October 5, 1932.
Mary died June 7, 1933, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, at the age of 21. Her death certificate identifies Frank Mathis as her husband.
At the time of Mary's death, Joseph was three years old and Honorine was approximately eight months old.
Emma E. Blanton was born around 1857, the daughter of Greenberry Blanton and Sarah M. Wadsworth.
She appears in the 1860 United States Census in Lowndes County, Georgia, at approximately three years of age. No later records have yet been identified confirming her adult life or date of death.

Greenberry Blanton, also recorded as Green Berry or Berry Blanton, was born May 25, 1829, according to the published family history Aldermans in America. That publication identifies his parents as David Blanton and Nancy Goff.
Greenberry married Sarah M. Wadsworth, also known as Sallie Wadsworth, on December 6, 1857, in Madison County, Florida.

In the 1860 United States Census, Greenberry was living in Lowndes County, Georgia, with his wife Sarah and two children, Emma E. Blanton and William T. Blanton. The census recorded his age as 31 and his birthplace as North Carolina.
Greenberry's whereabouts after the 1860 census remain uncertain. Aldermans in America reports that he died around 1863, but this date has not been independently verified.

A Confederate military index identifies a G. B. Blanton serving as a private in Company H, 26th Georgia Infantry. Although the name and geographic connection make this a possible match, no evidence has yet established that the soldier was Greenberry Blanton.

Sarah subsequently married Everett Darling on March 28, 1879, in Madison County, Florida. The 1880 census records a four-year-old girl named Liddy A. Blanton as Everett's stepdaughter. Liddy's biological father has not been established, and her relationship to Greenberry remains uncertain.
William T. Blanton was born around 1859, the son of Greenberry Blanton and Sarah M. Wadsworth.
He appears in the 1860 United States Census in Lowndes County, Georgia, at six months of age.
Family research indicates that William died in 1881. The source confirming his death has not yet been added to the archive.

An Eliza Branch, age two, appears in the 1860 United States Census in Ware County, Georgia, in the household of Henry and Mary Branch. Mary Branch may have been Mary Ann Adkinson, born about 1837, who appears in the 1850 census of Laurens County, Georgia. The identification of these individuals as Elizabeth Branch's parents and maternal grandparents remains unconfirmed.
John Waters Bryan was born on February 7, 1829, in Georgia. His birth and death dates are recorded on his gravestone at Fort White City Cemetery in Columbia County, Florida.

The 1850 United States Census records a John W. Bryant, age 21, working as a merchant and living in Pike County, Georgia, in the household of Alexander and Harriet Bryant. These individuals are believed to be John's parents, although the relationship requires further documentation.
John married Dolly Ann Leslie on January 2, 1853, in Spalding County, Georgia. Their original marriage record identifies the couple as John W. Bryan and Dolly Ann Leslie.
John and Dolly lived in Spalding County, Georgia, during the 1860 and 1870 censuses. Their household included several children. Their daughter Mary Evline Bryant was born about 1875.
John died on December 30, 1878, at the age of 49. He is buried in Fort White City Cemetery in Fort White, Columbia County, Florida.
Historical records use both Bryan and Bryant as spellings of the family surname.
Alec Bryant was born around 1869. In the 1880 United States Federal Census, Alec, age 11, was living with his mother, Dolly Bryant, and siblings Myram, Hattie, and Mary in Columbia County, Florida.
Hattie Bryant was born around 1873. In the 1880 United States Federal Census, Hattie, age 7, was living with her mother, Dolly Bryant, and siblings Myram, Alec, and Mary in Columbia County, Florida.

Mary Eveline Bryant Singletary was born in May 1875 in Florida, the daughter of John Waters Bryan (1829–1878) and Dolly Ann Leslie (born 1834). Her surname appears as both Bryan and Bryant in historical and family research records. Her middle name has also appeared with different spellings, including Evline. A cemetery survey conducted in May 1968 by Moseley and Verrill identifies her as Mary Eveline Singletary, providing documentary support for the spelling Eveline used in this biography.

Mary was the youngest of six known children. Her siblings were John Bryant (1854–1928), Amanda M. Bryan (born 1856), Myram D. Bryan (1859–1916), Alexander Eugene Bryan (1869–1901), and Hattie Bryan (1871–1885). Her father died in 1878, when Mary was approximately three years old. In the 1880 United States Federal Census, five-year-old Mary was living in Columbia County, Florida, with her widowed mother, Dolly Bryant, and siblings Myram, Alexander, and Hattie. The census provides an early record of Mary's childhood and the family's circumstances following her father's death.

On February 4, 1890, Mary Bryant married John Vershal Singletary in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license was issued on February 3, 1890, and the ceremony was performed by Reverend A. T. Wood. The marriage was recorded on March 3, 1890, in Lafayette County Marriage Record Book B, page 422. Mary was fourteen years old at the time of her marriage, while John was approximately thirty-eight. The couple established their home in Lafayette County, where John worked as a farmer.

Mary and John had six known children: Jessie Von Singletary (born 1891), Annie Evaline Singletary (1893–1951), George William Singletary Sr. (1895–1964), Albert Eugene Singletary (1899–1928), Alice Geneva Singletary (1904–1928), and Viola Singletary (1906–1987). Family research suggests that Jessie died relatively young, possibly during the 1910s, although his death date has not been independently verified. His original gravestone is located in the same cemetery as those of his parents.

The 1900 United States Federal Census recorded John and Mary living in Lafayette County with their four oldest children: Jessie, Annie, George, and Albert. Mary was recorded as twenty-five years old, born in May 1875. The couple reported ten years of marriage, consistent with their documented marriage in February 1890. Mary reported having given birth to four children, all four of whom were living. John continued to support the family through farming.

By the 1910 United States Federal Census, John and Mary's household included Annie, George, Albert, Alice, and Viola. Their oldest son, Jessie, then approximately eighteen or nineteen years old, was no longer living in the household. Mary reported having given birth to six children, all six of whom were living. This census is the last record examined during this research in which both John and Mary have been positively identified together.

The years following the 1910 census remain an important unanswered chapter in the family's history. A cemetery survey conducted in May 1968 recorded John V. Singletary's gravestone dates as 1859–1911, providing evidence that he died in 1911. Although the birth year of 1859 conflicts with earlier census records, particularly the 1860 census and the August 1851 birth date recorded in 1900, the death year of 1911 is provisionally accepted. No contemporary death certificate or other original death record has been located to independently confirm the date.

The 1920 United States Federal Census provides an important clue concerning the circumstances of the family after John's probable death. Their daughters Alice Geneva Singletary, approximately seventeen years old, and Viola Singletary, approximately fourteen years old, were living in the household of their older brother, George William Singletary, in Lafayette County, Florida. Both sisters were still minors. Their presence in George's household suggests that he may have assumed responsibility for his younger sisters following the death of their father and possibly their mother. However, the census does not establish whether George was their legal guardian or explain why the sisters were living with him.

Mary has not been positively identified in the 1920 census records examined during this research. Her absence from the household, together with the residence of her two youngest daughters with their older brother, provides circumstantial evidence that she may have died sometime between 1910 and 1920. It is also possible that her death occurred around the time of John's probable death in 1911, although no documentary evidence has been found to establish this. Other explanations for her absence from the household, including remarriage or residence elsewhere, cannot be ruled out. Despite efforts to locate a death certificate or other contemporary record, Mary's date and circumstances of death remain unknown.

Mary Eveline Bryant Singletary and John Vershal Singletary are buried at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, formerly known as Bell's Mill Creek Cemetery, in Day, Lafayette County, Florida. Their original grave markers remain at the cemetery, although the inscriptions have deteriorated considerably. A cemetery survey conducted in May 1968 by Moseley and Verrill identified Mary Eveline Singletary as the wife of John V. Singletary but recorded no birth or death dates for her. The survey provides valuable historical documentation of the cemetery inscriptions before further deterioration occurred. A photograph of Mary's original gravestone taken in spring 2026 shows that the inscription is now extremely difficult to read.

In 2011, their great-grandson Arthur Singletary Sr. installed an additional shared headstone commemorating John and Mary. The death dates inscribed on this newer memorial reflect family research and have not been independently verified through contemporary records. The original grave markers, the 1968 cemetery survey, and the additional memorial together preserve important evidence of the family's burial history while also illustrating the uncertainties that remain concerning John and Mary's deaths.
Myram Bryant was born around 1860. In the 1880 United States Federal Census, Myram, age 20, was living with his mother, Dolly Bryant, and siblings Alec, Hattie, and Mary in Columbia County, Florida.
Elizabeth Lesley was born about 1812 in Georgia. Her maiden surname has not yet been established.
The 1850 United States Census records Elizabeth, age 38, living in District 68 of Pike County, Georgia, in the household of James M. Lesley.
The household included D. A. Lesley, age 15, who is believed to be Dolly Ann Leslie, the future wife of John Waters Bryan.
Elizabeth and James are considered probable parents of Dolly Ann Leslie, although additional documentation is needed to confirm the relationship.

death_place: Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, United States
biography: Everett Darling was born April 14, 1854, in Connecticut. According to a family account provided by his granddaughter Bettie Darling Prestridge, Everett experienced a difficult childhood. He was reportedly given away as an infant and raised in poorhouses and foster homes. His biological parents have not yet been conclusively identified.

Bettie related a story passed down through her father, James Darling, concerning Everett's discovery of his mother's identity. In 1875, Everett reportedly learned that a woman he had known for many years was actually his biological mother. Upset by this discovery, he decided to leave Connecticut and begin a new life in Florida.

According to the family story, Everett traveled by ship to Jacksonville, Florida, arriving on April 14, 1875, his twenty-first birthday. He subsequently moved inland to Madison County, Florida, where he established his home.

In 1879, Everett married Sarah Wadsworth Blanton, a widow who had children from her previous marriage. Everett and Sarah had two daughters together, Mary and Martha Darling. Their daughter Mary Frances Darling became an ancestor of the Singletary family.

Everett and Sarah remained married until Sarah's death in 1908. The following year, in 1909, Everett married Susan Lucinda Nipper. They had four children: William Everett Darling, born in 1911; Nettie Darling, born in 1914; James Darling, born in 1917; and John Jackson Darling, born in 1920.
Everett spent the remainder of his life in Florida. He died September 11, 1935, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, at the age of 81.

Bettie Darling Prestridge also cautioned against confusing her grandfather with another Everett Darling who appears in New England census records as the son of Moses Darling and Caroline Sharp. According to Bettie's research, that Everett was born in Massachusetts and remained in New England, while her grandfather was born in Connecticut and eventually settled in Florida. The parentage of Everett Darling of Mayo, Florida, therefore remains an unresolved genealogical question.
Mary Frances Darling was the wife of Daniel M. Mathis and the mother of Lela Mae Mathis. The family was living in Madison County, Florida, when the 1910 United States Census was recorded.

Willie Evans, also recorded as Will Evans, was born on July 9, 1887, according to the dates inscribed on his gravestone in Live Oak Cemetery, Live Oak, Florida. His birthplace and the identities of his parents have not yet been conclusively established. Federal census records provide differing information about his birthplace, identifying Florida in some years and Georgia in 1930.

On October 24, 1915, Willie married Emma Singletary (1895–1984), daughter of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary and Ida Alla Miller Singletary, in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license was issued on October 23, 1915, in Mayo, and the marriage was recorded on November 13 in Marriage Record Book E, page 166. The marriage record identifies him as Will Evans.

By January 1920, Willie and Emma were living in Precinct 8 of Suwannee County, Florida, in the Dowling Park area. The federal census recorded Willie, age 32, as head of household and employed in a sawmill. Emma and their infant son Ernest Evans, approximately three months old, were also enumerated in the household.

Dowling Park was an important center of the northern Florida lumber industry during the early twentieth century. Sawmills, timber operations, and railroad connections shaped the community and provided employment for local families. Willie's occupation placed him within this regional lumber economy, although the available records do not identify his specific employer.

In April 1930, Willie and Emma continued to live in the Dowling Park area of Suwannee County. The census recorded Willie, age 42, working as a laborer in a shingle or lath mill. Their children Ernest and Gracie were living with them. Emma's younger brother Jasper Singletary and his wife were enumerated in the preceding household, suggesting that the two families were close neighbors. The Evans family was recorded as renting its residence.

By April 1940, Willie and Emma had moved to Mayo in Lafayette County, Florida. The federal census recorded Willie E. Evans, age 52, as head of household. His wife Emma, their sons Ernest and Frederick, and their daughter Gracie were living with him. Also in the household was Gracie's husband, Owen Lassiter, identified as Willie's son-in-law. This census provides a particularly useful record of the family together during their adult children's early years.

In April 1950, Willie and Emma were living in Suwannee County, Florida. Willie, age 62, was employed as a watchman at a wholesale planing mill, continuing his long association with the lumber industry. Emma, age 54, was listed as his wife, and no children or other relatives were enumerated in their household. The couple reported that they had lived in the same house one year earlier.

Willie and Emma had at least three children: Ernest Evans, Frederick Evans, also known as Fred, and Gracie Evans Lassiter, also known as Grace. The family's census records trace their lives between Lafayette and Suwannee counties and document Willie's employment in sawmill and lumber-related occupations over several decades.

Willie Evans died on October 7, 1971, at the age of 84. His obituary, published in The Florida Times-Union on October 9, 1971, identified his surviving wife, Emma; daughter Grace Lassiter of Palatka; and sons Ernest and Fred Evans of Jacksonville. He was also survived by four grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren. Funeral services were scheduled for October 9, 1971, at Westwood Baptist Church in Live Oak, Florida, with Harris Funeral Home handling the arrangements. Willie was buried in Live Oak Cemetery, where he shares a gravestone with Emma, who died in 1984.

birth_place: Clearwater, Pinellas County, Florida, United States
death_place: Dowling Park, Suwannee County, Florida, United States
biography: Debra Renee George was born on March 11, 1956, in Clearwater, Pinellas County, Florida. She was a daughter of Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011).
Debra was identified as Freddy Mathis's stepdaughter in his obituary published in The Florida Times-Union on December 21, 1967.
On January 31, 1981, Debra married Billy Franklin Odom in Taylor County, Florida. Their marriage is documented in Florida Department of Health records under certificate number 014688.
Debra was also known as Debra Renee Cotrel. The circumstances and date of her adoption of the Cotrel surname have not yet been established.
Debra died on June 27, 2012, in Dowling Park, Suwannee County, Florida, at the age of 56. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida.
John S. George was married to Evelyn Herrin.
Florida divorce records identify Evelyn Y. George and John S. George as divorcing in Pinellas County, Florida, in October 1968. The divorce was recorded under certificate number 25814.
John's birth and death dates have not yet been established.

Rachel Griffin was born in Georgia around March 1850. In August 1850, she was enumerated in District 81 of Thomas County, Georgia, in the household of John and Eliza Griffin. The census recorded her age as five months. Her 1935 death certificate independently identifies John Griffin as her father, providing additional evidence connecting Rachel to this household.

On October 14, 1869, Rachel married Simon P. Singletary in Decatur County, Georgia. Their marriage is documented in the original county marriage register. Her husband appears in other historical records as Silas P. Singletary and S. P. Singletary.

In 1870, Rachel was living in Decatur County, Georgia, in the household of Jacob Singletary. The federal census recorded her as eighteen years old. Her presence alongside Silas Singletary, whom she had married the previous year, provides additional evidence connecting the marriage record to the Singletary family.

By June 1900, Rachel and Silas were living in Thomas County, Georgia. The federal census identified Rachel as Silas's wife and recorded four children in their household: Emma P., Mary, Robert, and Dollie Singletary.
Rachel's husband, Silas P. Singletary, died on January 10, 1915, according to his burial record. He was buried at Springhill Christian Church Cemetery near Ochlocknee, Thomas County, Georgia.

In 1916, Rachel applied for a Confederate widow's pension in Thomas County, Georgia, based on her late husband's military service. Her application, preserved in the Georgia Archives, identifies her husband as S. P. Singletary and provides information about their marriage. The pension documents also contain a handwritten statement concerning differences in recollections of the couple's marriage. Their marriage is independently documented in the original Decatur County marriage register dated October 14, 1869.

Rachel died on June 28, 1935, in Ochlocknee, Thomas County, Georgia. Her Georgia death certificate records her age as ninety-five, suggesting a birth around 1840. However, the 1850 federal census recorded her as five months old, suggesting a birth around March 1850. The earlier census provides stronger evidence for her approximate birth year, although the discrepancy remains unresolved.

Rachel's death certificate identifies her father as John Griffin and records a mother's maiden name that has not yet been conclusively deciphered. The certificate lists chronic nephritis and senility among the causes of death. Rachel was buried on June 29, 1935, at Springhill Cemetery near Ochlocknee, Georgia.
Daniel Herrin was reportedly born around 1810, the son of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
According to family research, Daniel married Mehala Kelly and later Jemina Ammons.
Daniel's death date and burial location have not yet been established.
Deloris Herrin was born in 1942 in Lafayette County, Florida. She is a daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer.
Dorothy Herrin was born on December 27, 1929, in Georgia.
She was a daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. She died on June 6, 2021, in Florida.
Evelyn Herrin was born on September 14, 1934, in Pearson, Atkinson County, Georgia.

In 1945, Evelyn was living with her parents, William Levi and Laura Etta Herrin, on Route 2 near Mayo in Lafayette County, Florida. The Florida State Census recorded Evelyn as a ten-year-old student living with several of her brothers and sisters. A surviving school portrait from the 1950–1951 school year further documents her connection to Mayo during her teenage years.
Evelyn spent part of her youth in Lafayette County, Florida. A surviving school portrait from the 1950–1951 school year identifies Mayo, Florida, as the location of her school photograph.
She was a daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. She died on February 19, 2011, in Florida.

During her lifetime, Evelyn married Freddy Ray Mathis (1938–1967), John S. George, and David Brewer Webb (1942–2007). Florida divorce records document her divorce from John S. George in Pinellas County in October 1968 and from David Webb in Taylor County on June 6, 1975.

Evelyn died on February 19, 2011, in Perry, Taylor County, Florida, at the age of 76. She is buried at Waters Memorial Gardens in Steinhatchee, Florida, where a shared memorial commemorates her and David 'Buddy' Webb (1941–2007). The marker also names Stevie, Ricky, Connie Ray, and Debra as their children.
Gladys Lucille Herrin was born May 25, 1924, in Clinch County, Georgia, the daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer.
On August 3, 1947, Gladys married Lamar Lee Stephens in Brooks County, Georgia. The ceremony was performed by Frank H. McElroy, a minister.

Interestingly, Gladys's sister Marylou Herrin married Gordon Edward Bell on the same day, August 3, 1947, in Brooks County. Both marriages were performed by the same minister, Frank H. McElroy, and their marriage certificates appear together in the county marriage register. Whether the sisters participated in a joint wedding ceremony has not yet been established.
Gladys lived in Taylor County, Florida. She died September 27, 1954, at her home in Foley, Florida, at age 30.
Her death certificate identifies cardiorespiratory failure due to status asthmaticus as the cause of death.
Gladys was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida.
Heron Herrin was born around 1770 in North Carolina. Family research identifies him by the nickname Mack, although contemporary documentation confirming this name has not yet been located.

In September 1799, a land warrant was issued for 400 acres in Glynn County, Georgia, to a man recorded as Heron Herron. A corresponding land grant was issued in 1800. These records are consistent with the account preserved in family research.

According to research compiled by Arthur Singletary Sr., Heron moved to Camden County, Georgia, around 1811 and worked as a farm overseer for Burwell Atkinson. The research states that Atkinson killed Heron during an argument in 1817 and was subsequently tried for murder. The original court proceedings have not yet been examined.
Heron and his wife Ann reportedly had seven children: Olive, John, Nancy, James, Levi, William, and Daniel Herrin.
Family research suggests that Heron may have been the son of Enoch Herin, but this relationship remains unverified.

Ida Mae Herrin, affectionately known as Shorty, was born on January 2, 1922, in Homerville, Clinch County, Georgia. She was the daughter of William Levi Herrin and Lauretta (Laura Etta) Palmer Herrin. Her gravestone records her birth year as 1922, while a Social Security application and claims record gives January 2, 1923. This discrepancy has not yet been resolved.

On April 17, 1942, Ida Mae married Hope Sullivan in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage is documented in a Florida marriage index. Eight children with the Sullivan surname, or a married variation of it, are listed on Ida Mae's later gravestone: Stella S. Osborn, Nell Sullivan, Connie Mack Sullivan, Billy Sullivan, Wayland Sullivan, Mike Sullivan, Jack Sullivan, and Drew Sullivan. Their individual parentage and birth dates have not yet been independently verified.

On April 5, 1959, Ida Mae married Lawrence M. Secreast. A Florida marriage index records the marriage in Wakulla County in April 1959, and their shared gravestone supplies the exact date. Lawrence was born on February 18, 1912, and died on June 3, 1982.

Ida Mae died on July 14, 2003, in Fanning Springs, Gilchrist County, Florida, at the age of 81. She was buried at Old Town Memorial Cemetery in Old Town, Dixie County, Florida, alongside her husband Lawrence M. Secreast. Their shared gravestone commemorates their marriage on April 5, 1959, and lists eight children.
James Herrin was reportedly born in North Carolina around 1800, the son of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
According to family research, James married Mary Rooks, daughter of John Rooks, on June 10, 1827.
Family research indicates that James lived beyond 1880. His exact death date and burial location have not yet been established.

death_place: Lake City, Columbia, Florida, United States
biography: James Talmadge Herrin was born November 12, 1919, in Georgia. His obituary identifies Homerville, Georgia, as his birthplace. He was a son of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer.

During World War II, James served in the United States Army. His military gravestone identifies him as a World War II veteran, although his unit, rank, and dates of service have not yet been established.
James married Myrtis Hurst on October 13, 1945, in Echols County, Georgia.
James lived in Perry, Taylor County, Florida, for most of his life. He worked in the dairy business and later for Dan Stewart Gulf Stream Crab Company.
James died February 8, 1986, at the Veterans Administration Medical Center in Lake City, Florida, at age 66.
His obituary identifies four daughters, Diane Dodge, Pat La Blanc, Janet Dekyne, and Tonya Herrin, and two sons, William Herrin and James Herrin Jr.
James was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida.
John Herrin was reportedly born in North Carolina around 1795, the son of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
According to family research, John married Ann Clements, daughter of William Clements.
John reportedly died around 1820. His death location and the circumstances of his death have not yet been established.
Levi Herrin was born on July 8, 1804, in Georgia. He was the son of Herron Herrin and Ann D., according to the family records currently collected.
Levi married Charity Sears, who was born on October 28, 1812. Together, they raised a family in southern Georgia during a period of significant settlement and development.

Among their children were William M. Herrin and Charlotte Herrin. These two children established separate branches of the family that would eventually reconnect through the marriage of their descendants.

William M. Herrin's grandson, William Levi Herrin (1892–1975), married Charlotte Herrin's granddaughter, Laura Etta Palmer (1898–1959), in April 1916 in Clinch County, Georgia. They were third cousins through their common ancestors, Levi Herrin and Charity Sears.
Family records identify possible Confederate military service during the American Civil War as a private in Company I, 50th Georgia Infantry. This service has not yet been independently verified.
Levi died on September 29, 1890, in Millwood, Clinch County, Georgia, at the age of 86.

Mary Lou Herrin was born May 8, 1927, in Pearson, Atkinson County, Georgia, the daughter of William Levi Herrin (1892–1975) and Laura Etta Palmer (1898–1959). She grew up as part of the large Herrin family, whose roots extended through southern Georgia and northern Florida.

On August 3, 1947, at age 20, Mary Lou married Gordon Edward Bell in Brooks County, Georgia. Their marriage was performed by Frank H. McElroy, a minister. An unusual family connection occurred that same day when Mary Lou's sister Gladys Lucille Herrin married Lamar Lee Stephens, also in Brooks County, with the same minister officiating. The sisters' marriage records appear together on the same page of the county marriage register. Although it is not known whether they participated in a joint wedding ceremony, the two sisters shared the same wedding date and minister.

In 1952, Mary Lou married Charles Alton Miller Sr. (1929–2015) in Taylor County, Florida. The Florida Department of Health marriage record identifies her as Mary Lou Bell, reflecting her surname from her previous marriage. Their marriage was recorded under certificate number 15947, volume 1387.

Mary Lou and Charles had two children, Robbie and Linda Miller. A family photograph shows Mary Lou seated with her children in front of a Christmas tree, preserving a glimpse of their family life. Linda is believed to be the Linda T. Miller identified as the informant on Mary Lou's death certificate, although that connection has not yet been independently verified.

Mary Lou and Charles Miller divorced in June 1967 in Taylor County, Florida. Their divorce is documented in Florida records under certificate number 13840. Charles later died January 18, 2015, in Florida, at age 85.

Following her divorce, Mary Lou married Howard Mathis. Howard was the brother of Freddy Ray Mathis, who married Mary Lou's sister Evelyn Herrin. As a result, two Herrin sisters married two Mathis brothers, creating an additional family connection between the Herrin and Mathis families. The exact date and location of Mary Lou's marriage to Howard have not yet been established.

Mary Lou spent part of her life in Taylor County, Florida, where several members of the Herrin family had settled. Her death certificate identifies her occupation as homemaker and records Howard Mathis as her surviving husband.

Mary Lou died December 16, 1972, in Orlando, Orange County, Florida, at the age of 45. Her death certificate identifies Miss Linda T. Miller as the informant. She was buried December 19, 1972, at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida, where several members of the Herrin family are also buried.
Nancy Herrin was reportedly born in North Carolina around 1798, the daughter of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
According to family research, Nancy married Solomon Robeson on September 6, 1818.
Nancy is believed to have died before 1830. Her exact death date and burial location remain unknown.
Olive Herrin was reportedly born in North Carolina around 1793. According to family research, she was a daughter of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
Olive reportedly married Moses Turner in 1810. Family research indicates that the couple moved to Hamilton County, Florida, following their marriage.
Olive is reported to have died in Wayne County, Georgia, around 1830. These details remain to be verified against historical records.

birth_place: Homerville, Clinch County, Georgia, United States
biography: Ollie Mae Herrin was born on September 6, 1917, in Homerville, Clinch County, Georgia, the oldest child of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. As a young child she was recorded as Ollie Clayton, a name she did not like and later replaced in everyday use with Ollie Mae. By 1940, contemporary records were consistently identifying her as Ollie Mae.

Ollie spent her childhood in south Georgia as her parents' family steadily grew. The 1920 census found her with her parents and younger brother James Talmage in Clinch County. By 1930, the family was living in Pearson, Atkinson County, and included six children. During the 1930s the Herrin family moved from Georgia to Lafayette County, Florida, where the 1940 census recorded Ollie Mae, then 22, still living with her parents and younger siblings.

On June 21, 1940, Ollie Mae married Dewey Singletary in Lafayette County, Florida. They established their home in the Mayo area. The 1945 Florida State Census records Ollie and Dewey with their four-year-old son Arthur. Dewey was working as a laborer, while Ollie was recorded as a housewife. By 1950, their family had grown with the birth of another son, Emory, and Dewey was working as an automobile mechanic.

In 1955, Ollie Mae and Dewey experienced the loss of their son James Loyd, who was stillborn at Tallahassee Memorial Hospital. Surviving records disagree slightly on the exact date, with evidence indicating September 24 or September 25.
Ollie Mae and Dewey eventually made their home in the Perry area. Dewey died in 1973, leaving Ollie a widow. Ollie remained in Perry for the rest of her life.

Ollie Mae Singletary died at Doctors Memorial Hospital in Perry on June 7, 1992, at the age of 74. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, where other members of the Herrin and Singletary families are also buried.
Shelby Jean Herrin was born February 26, 1939, in Clinch County, Georgia. She was a daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer.
Shelby married Arthur M. Freeman and lived in Stockbridge, Henry County, Georgia. Her occupation was recorded as key punch operator.
Shelby died September 12, 1978, at Clayton General Hospital in Riverdale, Clayton County, Georgia, at age 39.

Her obituary identifies her husband, Arthur M. Freeman, and daughter, Elizabeth Renea Griffin. It also names her surviving siblings: Ollie Singletary, Evelyn Webb, Ida Mae Seacrest, Dorothy Hines, Deloris Morgan, James Herrin, and Billy Herrin.
Shelby was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida.

Thomas Levi Herrin married Elizabeth Branch on February 11, 1878, in Ware County, Georgia. Their marriage was performed by Thomas Brabham, a preacher of the Gospel. The original marriage certificate records his surname as Herring. Elizabeth was Thomas's first wife. He later married Nancy T. Jewell, with whom he had his son William Levi Herrin (1892–1975).
William Herrin was reportedly born in North Carolina around 1806, the son of Heron Herrin and Ann D.
According to family research, William married Barshaba Lindsay around 1826. The couple subsequently moved to Columbia County, Florida.
William reportedly died in Columbia County, Florida, around 1888. Additional historical records are needed to verify these details.

William Levi Herrin was born on May 4, 1892, in Clinch County, Georgia, the son of Thomas Levi Herrin and Nancy T. Jewell. He grew up in south Georgia and as a young man married Laura Etta Palmer of Pearson, Georgia. Together they would raise a large family of ten children.

In June 1917, William registered for the World War I draft in Clinch County, Georgia. At age 25, he was living on Rural Free Delivery Route 2 near Pearson, Georgia, and working as a farmer. He reported that he was married and that his wife depended upon him for support. The registrar described William as being of medium height and build, with blue eyes and dark hair. He reported no previous military service. His draft registration does not establish that he subsequently served in the armed forces.

By 1920, William and Laura Etta were living in Clinch County with their first two children, Ollie Clayton and James Talmage. William was working as a farmer on a general farm. During the following decade the family moved to the Pearson area of Atkinson County, Georgia. By 1930, William and Laura owned their home and were raising six children: Ollie, James, Ida Mae, Gladys, Mary Lou, and Dorothy. William continued to support his growing family through farming.

The family continued to grow during the 1930s with the births of William "Billy," Evelyn, and Shelby Jean. By 1940, William and Laura Etta had moved their family from Georgia to Lafayette County, Florida. Their tenth and youngest child, Deloris, was born in Florida in 1942. The 1950 census found William and Laura Etta still in Lafayette County, with five of their younger children remaining at home. William, then 58, was still working as a farmer.

Farming was a major part of William's working life, but in his later years he also worked in the logging and sawmill business. In 1954, he moved from Mayo to Perry, Florida. Laura Etta died in 1959, leaving William a widower after more than four decades of marriage.

William remained in the Perry area for the rest of his life and was a member of the Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints. He died at Doctors Memorial Hospital in Perry on March 12, 1975, at the age of 82. He was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, where Laura Etta had been buried sixteen years earlier.

By the time of William's death, the family he and Laura Etta had begun many decades earlier had grown considerably. His obituary reported eight surviving children, 28 grandchildren, and 28 great-grandchildren.
William Levi Herrin was born on May 10, 1932, in Pearson, Atkinson County, Georgia.
Known as "Billy," he was a son of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. He died on July 19, 1988, in Salem, Marion County, Oregon.
James M. Lesley was born about 1809 in Georgia. He is a probable father of Dolly Ann Leslie Bryan, based on the 1850 United States Census.
In September 1850, James was living in District 68 of Pike County, Georgia, with Elizabeth Lesley and five younger household members, including D. A. Lesley, age 15.
James was employed as a brick mason and reported real estate valued at $1,000.
The household is believed to represent James, his wife Elizabeth, and their children. However, the 1850 census did not record family relationships, so these connections remain provisional.
Dolly Ann Leslie was born in Georgia, probably during the mid-1830s. Historical census records give varying ages, suggesting birth years between approximately 1834 and 1840.
Dolly married John W. Bryan on January 2, 1853, in Spalding County, Georgia. Their original marriage record confirms the date and location.
The 1860 United States Census records Dolly, age 24, living with John and several children in Spalding County, Georgia. The family remained in Spalding County in 1870.

Following John's death in December 1878, Dolly appears as a widow in the 1880 United States Census in Columbia County, Florida. Her household included her daughter Mary Bryant, age five, along with other children.

A Savannah, Georgia, death record documents the death of Mrs. D. A. Bryan on June 6, 1906, at Telfair Hospital. The record gives her age as 72 and identifies Laurel Grove as her burial location. A Find a Grave memorial identifies this woman as Dolly Ann Leslie Bryan.
Dolly is memorialized at Laurel Grove Cemetery North in Savannah, Chatham County, Georgia. Her Find a Grave memorial identifies plot 0-0-1110-X6.

The 1850 United States Census records a 15-year-old D. A. Lesley living with James M. Lesley and Elizabeth Lesley in Pike County, Georgia. This individual is believed to be Dolly Ann Leslie, who married John W. Bryan in 1853. James and Elizabeth are therefore considered Dolly's probable parents, although the relationship has not been independently confirmed.
Connie Ray Mathis is the son of Freddy Ray Mathis (1938–1967) and Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011).
He is one of four children named on the memorial of Evelyn Herrin and David Brewer Webb at Waters Memorial Gardens in Steinhatchee, Florida.

Daniel M. Mathis was born on December 13, 1873, according to his World War I draft registration. He married Mary Frances Darling on January 1, 1899, in Madison County, Florida. By 1918, Daniel was living in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, where he worked as a farmer.
Frank Mathis was born April 30, 1907, in Madison County, Florida, the son of Daniel Mathis and Mary Frances Darling. He was a brother of Lela Mae Mathis.

Frank married his first wife, Mary Virginia Allen (1911–1933), on December 24, 1927, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. The ceremony was performed by County Judge Moses H. Padgett. Because Mary was only 15 years old, her parents provided written consent for the marriage. Frank and Mary had two children, Joseph Henry Mathis (1930–2012) and Honorine Virginia Mathis (1932–2005), both born in Mayo, Florida. Mary died June 7, 1933, leaving Frank with two young children.
Frank later married Minnie Ola Redman. The couple lived in Sneads, Jackson County, Florida. Frank worked in a furniture mill before retiring and was a member of the Baptist Church of Sneads.

Frank died July 22, 1969, at Florida State Hospital in Chattahoochee, Gadsden County, Florida, at age 62. His obituary identified Minnie as his surviving wife, along with his two children and a stepson, John Wayne McQuaid.
He was buried at Mount Pleasant Cemetery in Chattahoochee, Gadsden County, Florida.
Freddy Ray Mathis was born on January 16, 1938.

In January 1956, at approximately 18 years of age, Freddy was serving as a private in the United States Marine Corps. Marine Corps muster rolls identify him as a recruit assigned to the 2nd Recruit Training Battalion at Marine Corps Recruit Depot Parris Island, South Carolina.
A 1956 Perry, Florida, city directory lists Freddy, under the name Freddie R. Mathis, as a member of the United States Marine Corps residing at 801 East Quail Street.
Freddy lived on the same street as Dewey and Ollie Singletary, who resided at 601 East Quail Street. Ollie was the older sister of Freddy's wife, Evelyn Herrin.

According to a family recollection, Freddy played basketball with a Arthur Singletary Sr., the son of Dewey and Ollie Singletary. Whether they played together on a school basketball team or recreationally in their neighborhood has not yet been established.
Freddy married Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011), daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. They had two sons, Connie Ray Mathis and Richard Mathis, known as Ricky.
Freddy died on December 19, 1967, at the age of 29. His obituary appeared in The Florida Times-Union on December 21, 1967. He was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida.
Honorine Virginia Mathis was born October 5, 1932, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, the daughter of Frank Mathis and Mary Virginia Allen. She was a sister of Joseph Henry Mathis.

Frank Mathis's 1969 obituary identifies his daughter as Honorine Barber, living in Camilla, Georgia. Later records identify her as Honorine Virginia Mathis Grimsley. The details and dates of her marriages have not yet been established.
Honorine died May 27, 2005, in Camilla, Mitchell County, Georgia, at age 72. She was buried at Mount Pleasant Cemetery in Chattahoochee, Gadsden County, Florida, where her father was also buried.
Joseph Henry Mathis was born April 19, 1930, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, the son of Frank Mathis and Mary Virginia Allen. He was a brother of Honorine Virginia Mathis.
Joseph served in the United States military and held the rank of Specialist. His branch of service and dates of service have not yet been established.
Joseph was living in Albany, Georgia, when his father's obituary was published in 1969.
He died March 12, 2012, in Albany, Dougherty County, Georgia, at age 81. He was buried at Andersonville National Cemetery in Andersonville, Macon County, Georgia.
Richard Mathis, known as Ricky, is the son of Freddy Ray Mathis (1938–1967) and Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011).
Ricky grew up in the Perry, Florida, area and attended Taylor County High School. He appears in school yearbook records from 1977 and 1979.
Ricky is the brother of Connie Ray Mathis.
Malachi M. Matthews was born around 1840. His Florida death certificate identifies his birthplace as Thomas County, Georgia, and his father as Daniel Mathis.
Malachi married Mary Williams on October 27, 1870, in Madison County, Florida. Their marriage is documented in the county marriage register.
Historical records use several variations of the family surname, including Matthews, Mathews, and Mathis. Malachi died on August 23, 1924, in Madison County, Florida.

Military records identify a soldier named Malachi Matthews, also recorded as Malicah or Malachai Matthews, who served as a private in Company D of the 2nd Florida Cavalry (Union) during the American Civil War. A federal pension index records an application filed in Florida on July 19, 1890, under application number 816825, with pension certificate number 665746. The matching name and military unit provide strong evidence connecting these records, although additional documentation is needed to confirm that the soldier was the same Malachi Matthews who lived in Madison County, Florida.

In the spring of 2026, a descendant visited Mount Olive Cemetery in Madison County, Florida, searching for Malachi's grave. Although his death certificate identifies Mount Olive Cemetery as his burial location, no headstone could be located. During the visit, a local resident recalled that the cemetery once contained wooden grave markers that had disappeared over time. It is possible that Malachi's grave was originally marked with wood, although this has not been confirmed.
Ida Alla Miller was born on May 28, 1873, according to her gravestone. Her birthplace and parents have not yet been established.

On April 16, 1890, Ida married Jacob A. Singletary in Lafayette County, Florida. Their original marriage record identifies the bride as Ida Alla Miller and the groom as Jacob A. Singletary. The marriage ceremony was performed by D. H. Ward, and the license was filed for record on April 26, 1890.
Ida was sixteen years old at the time of her marriage, based on the birth date recorded on her gravestone. Jacob was thirty-eight years old.
Her husband, Jacob A. Singletary, was a minister and is identified as Reverend Jacob Singletary on their shared gravestone.

Ida died on October 16, 1945. Her gravestone identifies her as Ally Ida Singletary, a variation of the name recorded in her marriage record. She is commemorated alongside her husband at Bell's Mill Creek Cemetery, also known as Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, in Day, Lafayette County, Florida.

Linda Miller was born December 13, 1953, in Georgia, the daughter of Charles Alton Miller Sr. and Mary Lou Herrin. Her mother was a daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer. Linda had a brother, Robert B. Miller, known as Robbie, and a stepbrother, Charles Miller Jr.

Linda's name appears differently in surviving family records. Her mother's 1972 obituary identifies her as Laura Linda Miller, while her 1973 marriage announcement and marriage record identify her as Linda Louise Miller. Family recollections suggest her original name may have been Linda Laura Miller. Her gravestone identifies her simply as Linda Miller. Her full birth name has not yet been established.

Linda graduated from the Florida School for the Deaf and Blind in St. Augustine, Florida, and later attended Florida State University. Both educational institutions were identified in the newspaper announcement of her marriage.

On July 29, 1973, Linda married Jeffrey Phillip Smith at Sierra-Norwood Baptist Church. Their marriage was announced in The Miami Herald on July 30, 1973. A separate marriage record gives August 5, 1973, and the reason for the difference between the recorded dates has not yet been established.

Linda and Jeffrey divorced October 30, 1989, in Broward County, Florida. According to family recollections, Jeffrey was Linda's only husband, and she was unmarried at the time of her death. No children have been identified from their marriage.

Linda died January 8, 2020, in Florida, at the age of 66. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry, Taylor County, Florida, beside her mother, Mary Lou Herrin. Her gravestone bears the inscription 'Much Love.'

Laura Etta Palmer was born on June 25, 1898, in Pearson, Georgia, the daughter of Henry Palmer and Laura Williams. She grew up in south Georgia and as a young woman married William Levi Herrin. Together they would raise a large family of ten children.

By 1920, Laura Etta and William were living in Clinch County with their first two children, Ollie Clayton and James Talmage. During the following decade, the family moved to the Pearson area of Atkinson County. By 1930, Laura Etta was raising six children at home: Ollie, James, Ida Mae, Gladys, Mary Lou, and Dorothy.

The family continued to grow with the births of William "Billy," Evelyn, and Shelby Jean during the 1930s. By 1940, Laura Etta and William had moved their family from Georgia to Lafayette County, Florida. Their youngest child, Deloris, was born in Florida in 1942. By 1950, the older children had begun establishing homes and families of their own, while Dorothy, Billy, Evelyn, Shelby Jean, and Deloris remained with their parents.

Laura Etta spent her later years in the Mayo and Perry areas of Florida. On July 3, 1959, she died at the Perry home of her daughter Ollie Mae and son-in-law Dewey Singletary. She was 61 years old. She was buried at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry.

Laura Etta's obituary provides a glimpse of the family she left behind. In addition to her husband and children, she had 21 grandchildren. Her surviving brothers included Elias Palmer of Pearson, Georgia, and Frank Palmer of Punta Gorda, Florida.
Minnie Ola Redman was married to Frank Mathis (1907–1969). The couple lived in Sneads, Jackson County, Florida. Minnie was identified as Frank's surviving wife in his 1969 obituary.
Charity Sears ]was born on October 28, 1812, in Georgia. She was the daughter of David Sears (1791–1879) and Levicy Nobles (1792–1868).

Albert Eugene Singletary was born in October 1898, according to the 1900 United States Federal Census. His 1928 Florida death certificate instead records his birth year as 1899 and identifies his birthplace as Lafayette County, Florida.
Albert was the son of John V. Singletary and Mary Bryant (Bryan). In 1900, he was living with his parents and siblings Jessie, Annie, and George in Lafayette County, Florida.
Albert worked as a farmer in Lafayette County. He was married to Dicie Stewart on August 31, 1919, in Lafayette County, according to a Florida marriage record.

Albert died in November 1928 at approximately 29 years of age from an accidental gunshot wound to the abdomen. His death certificate identifies the cause of death as an accidental gunshot wound and records his burial location as Midway Cemetery in Lafayette County, Florida.
Albert's full name was Albert Eugene Singletary. The 1900 Federal Census records his middle initial as E., while his death certificate appears to record L. This discrepancy has not yet been resolved.

Albert's death certificate identifies his father as John V. Singletary, born in South Carolina, and his mother as Mary Brian, born in Florida. The 1900 census records different parental birthplaces, so these details require further investigation.
Alice Singletary was born around 1905 in Florida. She was the daughter of John V. Singletary and Mary Bryant Singletary.
The 1910 United States Federal Census lists Alice, approximately five years old, living with her parents and siblings in Lafayette County, Florida.
Annie Singletary was born in May 1893 in Florida, according to the 1900 United States Federal Census. She was the daughter of John V. Singletary and Mary Bryant Singletary.
In 1900, Annie was living with her parents and siblings in Lafayette County, Florida.

biography: Arthur Singletary was born on February 24, 1941, into the Singletary and Herrin families of North Florida. His parents were Dewey Singletary and Ollie Mae Herrin.

During his early years, Arthur spent time working on the 400-acre farm owned by his maternal grandfather, William Levi Herrin. The farm was located south of Mayo, Florida, near Midway Baptist Church in Lafayette County. These experiences were part of his upbringing in rural North Florida and connected him to the family's agricultural heritage.

Arthur began his military career in September 1960 when he enlisted in the United States Marine Corps. After completing his initial four-year enlistment, he was honorably discharged on September 7, 1964.

In February 1965, Arthur reenlisted in the Marine Corps in Macon, Georgia, as a Sergeant (E-5), immediately returning to active duty. He continued advancing through the enlisted ranks and, according to family recollections, eventually attained the rank of Master Sergeant (E-8).

Arthur subsequently received a direct commission as a Second Lieutenant based on his enlisted experience, without attending Officer Candidate School. As a Marine who transitioned from enlisted service to commissioned officer status, he was known as a Mustang officer.
By July 1976, Arthur was serving as a Second Lieutenant at Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. That month, his family moved into Married Officer Quarters (MOQ) 3160.

Throughout his military career, Arthur served in intelligence and counterintelligence assignments. His service included duty associated with the Vietnam War, specialized military education, and numerous decorations and awards, including the Navy Commendation Medal.
Arthur continued advancing through the commissioned officer ranks and retired from the United States Marine Corps on April 30, 1986, having attained the rank of Major (O-4).

Dewey Singletary was born on August 23, 1919, in Lafayette County, Florida, the son of George William Singletary and Lela Mae Mathis Singletary. He grew up in rural North Florida, where his family lived in the Mayo area of Lafayette County.

Dewey appears in the 1920 United States Census as an infant living with his parents and other family members in Lafayette County. By the 1930 census, he was ten years old and living with his parents and younger siblings.

Dewey married Ollie Mae Herrin, the daughter of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer Herrin. Together, they raised a family that included their sons Arthur Singletary Sr. and Emory Dewey Singletary. Their son James Loyd Singletary was stillborn in 1955.

On October 16, 1940, at the age of 21, Dewey registered for the World War II draft in Lafayette County. His registration card identified Ollie Mae as his wife and listed his employer as a Works Progress Administration (WPA) project in Tallahassee, Florida. Although Dewey registered for the draft, no records confirming military service during World War II have been identified.

Dewey was a skilled mechanic who operated his own repair shop. According to family recollections, he was exceptionally good at his trade, but operating the business presented financial difficulties because some customers failed to pay for the work he performed. He eventually closed his shop and went to work for the Florida State Road Department, where he continued working as a mechanic.

Dewey and Ollie later made their home in Perry, Taylor County, Florida. Family photographs preserve memories of their life together, including gatherings with their sons and members of the extended Singletary and Herrin families.

Dewey died on November 19, 1973, at Doctors Memorial Hospital in Perry, Florida, at the age of 54. His death certificate identifies the cause of death as an acute myocardial infarction resulting from arteriosclerotic cardiovascular disease.
He was buried on November 21, 1973, at Woodlawn Cemetery in Perry. His wife, Ollie Mae, died on June 7, 1992, and is buried alongside him.

Dewey's life reflects the experiences of a North Florida family during the Great Depression and the decades that followed. His work as a mechanic, his years of employment with the State Road Department, and the family he raised with Ollie remain important parts of his story.

Eliza Singletary was born in South Carolina, although her exact birth date and maiden name have not been established. Historical records identify her as Eliza B. Singletary, Eliza Singletary, and Elizabeth Singletary. Her gravestone appears to identify her as Eliza L. Singletary. The differences in her recorded name and age have not been fully resolved.

In 1850, Eliza was living in Sumter District, South Carolina, in the household of Jacob Singletary, a farmer. The federal census recorded her as Eliza B. Singletary, age thirty-five. The household also included Silas P., Sarah R., Mary E., George M., Jane H., and Samuel J. Singletary.

By 1860, the family had relocated to Decatur County, Georgia. The federal census recorded Eliza as thirty-four years old and born in South Carolina. The household included several individuals previously recorded in South Carolina, along with John Singletary, age eight, and a younger Jacob Singletary, age seven, both born in Georgia.

In 1870, Eliza appears to have been recorded as Elizabeth Singletary, age forty-five, in the household of Jacob Singletary in Decatur County, Georgia. Other household members included Silas, Rachel, Sarah A., Mary E., John, and a younger Jacob Singletary.

By June 1880, Eliza was living in Lafayette County, Florida, where the federal census identified her as head of household, age fifty-four. Her household included Sarah Singletary, Mary E. Singletary, John V. Singletary, and Jacob Singletary. The record provides evidence that members of the family had moved from Georgia to northern Florida.

In 1900, Eliza was living in Lafayette County, Florida, in a household associated with William Johnson and Sarah Singletary Johnson. The census recorded her birth as May 1812 and her age as eighty-eight. These details conflict with several earlier census records, particularly those from 1860, 1870, and 1880, which suggest a birth around 1825–1826.

Eliza is buried at Bell's Mill Creek Cemetery, now known as Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, in Day, Lafayette County, Florida. Her gravestone bears the inscription 'ELIZA L. SINGLETARY / MOTHER OF / J. A. SINGLETARY / AT REST.' The inscription identifies her middle initial as L., although the 1850 federal census recorded her as Eliza B. Singletary. The identity of J. A. Singletary has not been conclusively established. The gravestone contains no birth or death dates, and Eliza's exact date of death remains unknown.

Emma Singletary Evans was born on August 24, 1895, in Lafayette County, Florida, the daughter of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary (1852–1931) and Ida Alla Miller Singletary (1873–1945). She grew up in a large family in northern Florida, where her father was a minister. Emma appears with her parents and siblings in the 1900 and 1910 United States federal censuses for Lafayette County. Her siblings included Eliza, Sallie, William Robert, Henry, Jasper, Jamie, and Giddy Singletary.

On October 24, 1915, Emma married Willie Evans (1887–1971) in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license was issued on October 23 in Mayo, and the marriage was recorded on November 13, 1915, in Marriage Record Book E, page 166. The couple began their married life during a period when the timber and lumber industries were important sources of employment throughout northern Florida.

By January 1920, Emma and Willie were living in Precinct 8 of Suwannee County, Florida, in the Dowling Park area. The federal census recorded Willie working in a sawmill and identified their infant son Ernest Evans, then approximately three months old. Emma was listed as Willie's wife. The age recorded for Emma in this census appears inconsistent with her established birth date.

Dowling Park had developed into a significant lumber-producing community around the turn of the twentieth century. Large sawmill operations and railroad connections supported the timber industry and provided employment for area residents. Willie worked in this industry, although the available records do not establish which lumber company employed him.

The family remained in the Dowling Park area in 1930. The federal census recorded Willie working in a shingle or lath mill and identified two children in the household, Ernest and Gracie Evans. Emma's younger brother Jasper Singletary was enumerated in the immediately preceding household with his wife. Their consecutive census entries suggest that Emma and Jasper lived near one another, illustrating the continuing connections among members of the extended Singletary family.

By April 1940, Emma and Willie were living in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. The federal census recorded their sons Ernest Evans, age 20, and Frederick Evans, age 16, in the household. Their daughter Gracie, age 18, was also living with them, along with her husband, Owen Lassiter, age 22. This record establishes that Gracie had married Owen Lassiter by 1940 and helps identify her as Grace Lassiter, the daughter named in Emma's obituary many years later.

In April 1950, Emma and Willie were again living in Suwannee County, Florida. The federal census recorded Willie, age 62, working as a watchman at a wholesale planing mill. Emma, age 54, was listed as his wife. No children were enumerated in their household, and the couple reported that they had been living in the same house one year earlier. Willie's continued employment in the lumber industry reflected an occupation that had supported the family for much of their married life.

Willie died on October 7, 1971, at the age of 84. Emma later lived in Palatka, Putnam County, Florida, where she resided for approximately thirteen years before her death. She was a member of Tabernacle Baptist Church.

Emma died on April 28, 1984, at Putnam Memorial Nursing Home in Palatka, Florida, following a lengthy illness. She was 88 years old. Her obituary identified her surviving children as Grace Lassiter of Palatka and Ernest Evans and Fred Evans of Jacksonville. It also named her sister Sallie Spies and brothers Giddy, Jammie, and Jasper Singletary. Emma was survived by ten grandchildren and twenty-five great-grandchildren.

Funeral services for Emma were held on April 30, 1984, at Westwood Baptist Church in Live Oak, Florida, with Reverend Lorace Cothron officiating. Harris Funeral Home handled the arrangements. She was buried in Live Oak Cemetery in Live Oak, Florida, where she shares a gravestone with her husband, Willie Evans. Their marriage of nearly fifty-six years and the records of their children and descendants form an important part of the Singletary family history.

Jacob Singletary was born in South Carolina around 1800–1804, according to information recorded in the United States federal censuses of 1850, 1860, and 1870. His exact birth date and the identities of his parents have not been established.

In 1850, Jacob was living in Sumter District, South Carolina, where the federal census recorded him as fifty years old and employed as a farmer. His household included Eliza B. Singletary, age thirty-five, and six younger family members: Silas P., Sarah R., Mary E., George M., Jane H., and Samuel J. Singletary.

By 1860, Jacob and his family had relocated to the 19th District of Decatur County, Georgia. The federal census recorded Jacob as fifty-six years old and born in South Carolina. His household included Eliza, Silas, Sarah, Mary, George, Harrietta, Samuel, John, and a younger Jacob Singletary. The birthplaces recorded for the younger household members suggest that the family moved from South Carolina to Georgia during the early 1850s.

The 1860 census included John Singletary, age eight, born in Georgia. John also appeared in Jacob's household in 1870. These records provide strong evidence connecting John Vershal Singletary to Jacob's family, although the censuses themselves do not explicitly identify their relationship.

In 1870, Jacob was living in District 720, also identified as the Jones District, in Decatur County, Georgia. The federal census recorded him as sixty-nine years old and born in South Carolina. His household included Elizabeth Singletary, Silas, Rachel, Sarah A., Mary E., John, and a younger Jacob Singletary.

Jacob's whereabouts after 1870 have not been established. By 1880, Eliza Singletary was living in Lafayette County, Florida, as head of a household that included John V. Singletary and other family members. Jacob's exact date and place of death remain unknown.

Reverend Jacob A. Singletary was born on March 15, 1852, reportedly in Bainbridge, Decatur County, Georgia, the son of Jacob Singletary and Eliza Singletary. His birth date is recorded on his gravestone, while his 1931 Florida death certificate confirms March 1852, although the handwritten day is difficult to distinguish. His birthplace is specifically identified as Bainbridge, Georgia, on the June 5, 1918, World War I draft registration completed by his son, William Robert Singletary. Jacob's death certificate independently identifies Georgia as his state of birth. Although no contemporary birth record has been located, the available evidence supports Bainbridge as his probable birthplace.

Jacob's parents were living in Sumter District, South Carolina, when the 1850 United States Federal Census was recorded. By 1860, the family had relocated to Decatur County, Georgia, where Jacob appeared in his parents' household at approximately seven years of age. The family's presence in Decatur County during his childhood is consistent with the birthplace reported by his son many years later.

In the 1870 United States Federal Census, Jacob was again enumerated in Decatur County, Georgia, in the household of his father, Jacob Singletary. By 1880, the family had relocated to Lafayette County, Florida, where Jacob was recorded as twenty years old in the household headed by his mother, Eliza Singletary. His reported age in the 1880 census differs from the birth year recorded on his gravestone and death certificate.

Jacob became a Baptist minister and was identified as Reverend Jacob Singletary on his gravestone. On January 30, 1890, Elder J. A. Singletary performed the marriage ceremony of William Johnson and Sarah R. Singletary in Lafayette County, Florida. Sarah was Jacob's sister, and the officiant was probably Reverend Jacob A. Singletary, although this identification has not been conclusively established.

On April 16, 1890, Jacob A. Singletary married Ida Alla Miller in Lafayette County, Florida. Their original marriage records identify Redden B. Hill as the county judge who issued the license and D. H. Ward as the person who performed the ceremony. The marriage was filed for record on April 26, 1890. Ida was born on May 28, 1873, according to their shared gravestone. Her name appears as Ida Alla Miller in the marriage record and as Ally Ida Singletary on the gravestone.

Jacob and Ida established their family in Lafayette County, Florida, where they raised at least eight children: Eliza E. Singletary, later Eliza Bell; Sarah 'Sallie' Singletary, later Sallie Spies; William Robert Singletary (1894–1961); Emma Singletary, later Emma Evans; Henry Singletary; Giddy Singletary; Jamie Singletary; and Jasper Singletary. Their identities are supported by federal census records and the February 1961 obituary of William Robert Singletary, which identifies seven surviving brothers and sisters. The available records have not yet established complete birth and death dates for all of the children.

The 1900 United States Federal Census records Jacob and Ida living in Lafayette County with five children: Eliza E., Sarah, Robert, Emma, and Henry. Robert, later identified as William Robert Singletary, was recorded as born in May 1894. Subsequent records contain conflicting information about his birth year, including a May 3, 1897, date on his 1918 draft registration. His death certificate and gravestone record May 3, 1894.

In April 1910, Jacob and Ida were living in Precinct 1 of Lafayette County, Florida, with several of their children, including Robert, Henry, Giddy, and Jamie. The same census page also records the household of Jacob's brother, John Vershal Singletary, and his family. Their appearance on the same enumeration page suggests that the two brothers and their families continued living in the same general community, although it does not establish that their homes were immediately adjacent.

The 1920 United States Federal Census records Jacob, age sixty-eight, and Ida, age forty-six, living in Lafayette County with six children: Sallie, Robert, Henry, Jasper, Jamie, and Giddie. This census provides important evidence for the younger sons, particularly Jasper, who was subsequently identified as a surviving brother in William Robert Singletary's 1961 obituary.

By the 1930 United States Federal Census, Jacob and Ida were still living in the Day community of Lafayette County. Jacob was recorded as approximately seventy-six years old and continued working as a farmer. Their household included several adult children, among them William Robert, Henry, Jamie, and Giddie. The census recorded William Robert, Henry, and Jamie as sawmill laborers, while Giddie worked as a farm laborer. The household was enumerated on April 7, 1930, approximately thirteen months before Jacob's death.

Jacob's occupation was also recorded as farmer on his Florida death certificate. He died on May 14, 1931, in Lafayette County, Florida, at the age of seventy-nine. His death certificate records heart trouble as the cause of death. His parents' names were not provided by the informant, but their identities are established through earlier census records.

Reverend Jacob A. Singletary was buried at Bell's Mill Creek Cemetery, also known as Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, near Day in Lafayette County, Florida. His shared gravestone records his birth on March 15, 1852, and death on May 14, 1931. The same marker commemorates his wife, Ally Ida Singletary, who was born on May 28, 1873, and died on October 16, 1945.

Following Jacob's death, Ida continued living in Lafayette County. The 1940 United States Federal Census records her as a sixty-six-year-old widow living with their sons Robert, Henry, and Giddy, and their widowed daughter Sally Spies. This record documents the family's continued presence in the community nearly a decade after Jacob's death and five years before Ida's death.
