biography: James Loyd Singletary was the son of Dewey Singletary and Ollie Mae Herrin. He was stillborn in Tallahassee, Florida, in September 1955. Surviving records disagree slightly on the exact date, with evidence indicating September 24 or September 25.
James Loyd was buried at Airline Baptist Church Cemetery in Mayo, Florida.

Jasper Eugene Singletary was born on March 18, 1902, in Suwannee County, Florida, according to his World War II draft registration dated February 16, 1942. He was a son of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary (1852–1931) and Ida Alla Miller Singletary (1873–1945). Jasper grew up in the extended Singletary family of northern Florida, which included his siblings Eliza, Sallie, William Robert, Emma, Henry, Jamie, and Giddy Singletary.

The 1920 United States Federal Census records Jasper, age 18, living in Lafayette County, Florida, in the household of his parents, Jacob and Ida Singletary. Several of his siblings were also living in the family household at that time.

In 1927, Jasper Singletary married Amojine Landen in Suwannee County, Florida. Their marriage is recorded in the Florida Department of Health marriage index under certificate number 6071, volume 20. Jasper's 1942 World War II draft registration later identified Amogine Singletary as his next of kin, providing additional evidence of their relationship.

By April 1930, Jasper was living in the Dowling Park community of Suwannee County, Florida. He was enumerated in the household immediately preceding that of his sister Emma Singletary Evans and her husband, Willie Evans. Their consecutive census entries suggest that Jasper and Emma lived near one another during this period. The 1930 census also identifies a woman in Jasper's household whose name requires further verification.

On February 16, 1942, Jasper registered for the World War II draft in Live Oak, Suwannee County, Florida. His registration recorded his full name as Jasper Eugene Singletary, his date of birth as March 18, 1902, and his birthplace as Suwannee County, Florida. He was living in Live Oak and identified himself as his own employer. The registration named Amogine Singletary as his next of kin.

Jasper's draft registration described him as five feet eleven inches tall, weighing 150 pounds, with brown hair, brown eyes, and a ruddy complexion. Although the registration provides valuable biographical information, it does not establish that Jasper served in the military.

Jasper was named among the surviving brothers in the February 1961 obituary of William Robert Singletary and again in the April 1984 obituary and funeral memorial of his sister Emma Singletary Evans. At the time of Emma's death, Jasper was reported to be living in Live Oak, Florida. His date and place of death have not yet been established.

Jessie Von Singletary was born in 1891, the eldest known child of John Vershal Singletary and Mary Evline Bryant. He appeared with his parents in the 1900 United States Federal Census in Lafayette County, Florida. Jessie was no longer living in his parents' household in 1910 and has not been positively identified in subsequent records. He is buried at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery in Day, Lafayette County, Florida, where his apparently original gravestone is similar in appearance to the original markers of his parents. Family research suggests that Jessie died young, possibly between 1910 and 1920, although his exact death date has not been established.

John Vershal Singletary was born in Georgia, probably during the early 1850s. The 1900 United States Federal Census records his birth as August 1851, although his reported age varies considerably among census records. Family research identifies his parents as Jacob and Eliza Singletary. John spent his early years in southern Georgia before settling in Lafayette County, Florida.

In 1870, John was living in Decatur County, Georgia, in a household headed by Jacob Singletary. The census recorded John as sixteen years old and identified his occupation as farm laborer. Other members of the household included Elizabeth Singletary and several younger family members. The household provides an important connection between John's early life in Georgia and the Singletary family that later settled in northern Florida.

By June 1880, John was living in Lafayette County, Florida. The United States Federal Census, enumerated on June 25, listed Eliza Singletary as head of household, age fifty-four. Also living in the household were Sarah Singletary, age twenty-four; Mary E. Singletary, age twenty-two; John V. Singletary, age twenty-one; and Jacob Singletary, age twenty. Family research identifies these younger household members as John's siblings. The census establishes that John and members of his family had settled in Lafayette County by 1880.

John established himself as a farmer in Lafayette County. In 1882, the Florida State Gazetteer listed him among the county's prominent farmers and recorded that he owned forty acres of land in the Bula community. The Bula post office was located at Irvin's Ferry on the Old Luraville Road, approximately four miles from Mayo, Florida.

On February 4, 1890, John married Mary Bryant in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license had been issued on February 3, and the ceremony was performed by Reverend A. T. Wood. The marriage was recorded on March 3, 1890, in Lafayette County Marriage Record Book B, page 422. Mary's surname appears as both Bryant and Bryan in historical and family records. She was born in Florida in May 1875, according to the 1900 census.

John and Mary raised a family in Lafayette County. Their children included Jessie Von Singletary, Annie Evaline Singletary, George William Singletary, Albert Eugene Singletary, Alice Geneva Singletary, and Viola Singletary. The 1900 United States Federal Census recorded John as a farmer living with Mary and their four oldest children: Jessie, Annie, George, and Albert. The census reported that John was born in August 1851 and that the couple had been married for ten years.

The family continued living in Lafayette County during the early twentieth century. By the time of the 1910 Federal Census, John and Mary had six children, including their younger daughters Alice and Viola. John's reported age in the 1910 census differs from his age in earlier records, leaving his exact birth year uncertain.

John's later years and exact date of death have not been established. He and Mary appear in the 1910 Federal Census, but their circumstances after that time remain uncertain. In January 1920, their son George William Singletary, then twenty-four years old, was living in Lafayette County with his wife Lela, their infant son Dewey, and George's younger sisters Alice and Viola. Alice was seventeen years old and Viola was fourteen. Their presence in George's household suggests that he had assumed responsibility for helping care for his younger siblings, although the circumstances leading to this arrangement are unknown.

John Vershal Singletary and Mary Evline Bryant Singletary are buried at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, formerly known as Bell's Mill Creek Cemetery, in Day, Lafayette County, Florida. Their original grave markers remain at the cemetery. In 2011, an additional shared headstone was installed by their great-grandson, Arthur Singletary. The death dates inscribed on that memorial reflect family research and have not been independently verified. John's exact date of death therefore remains unknown.

A cemetery survey conducted in May 1968 by Moseley and Verrill at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery in Lafayette County, Florida, recorded John V. Singletary's gravestone dates as 1859–1911. A photograph of the original gravestone taken in spring 2026 shows a heavily weathered inscription, although the birth year 1859 remains partially legible. The 1968 transcription provides important evidence that John died in 1911. His recorded birth year of 1859 conflicts with earlier census records, particularly the 1860 census, which establishes that he was already living before 1859. The 1900 census records his birth as August 1851. His probable birth year is therefore retained as 1851, while 1911 is provisionally accepted as his death year.

birth_place: Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida, United States
death_place: Jacksonville, Duval County, Florida, United States
biography: Loyd McCoy Singletary was born on May 19, 1924, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. He was the son of George William Singletary and Lela Mae Mathis. Loyd grew up in the Mayo area as part of a large Singletary family that included his brothers Louie, Vershal, Dewey, and Bill, along with three sisters.

On June 30, 1942, shortly after his eighteenth birthday, Loyd registered for the military draft in Lafayette County, Florida. At the time, he was living in Mayo and listed his father, George Singletary, as his employer. His registration card described him as approximately five feet nine inches tall, weighing 115 pounds, with blue eyes and brown hair.

Loyd entered the United States Navy in May 1943 during World War II. A Navy muster roll records his enlistment on May 18, 1943, at Jacksonville, Florida, although a separate military index reports May 25, 1943.

On November 15, 1943, Loyd was received aboard USS Darby (DE-218), a destroyer escort, after assignment at the Naval Training Station in Norfolk, Virginia. At that time, his rating was Seaman Second Class. Another military record identifies him with USS Darby on October 1, 1945, documenting his association with the vessel at two points during the war.
Loyd served in the United States Naval Reserve and attained the rating of Seaman First Class, as recorded on his military gravestone. He was discharged from the Navy on November 26, 1945.

On February 10, 1946, Loyd married Nina Mae Phillips in Echols County, Georgia. Their marriage took place less than three months after his discharge from the Navy. The couple had four children: Fay, Derenda, Paul, and Joe.

Following World War II, Loyd settled with his family in Jacksonville, Florida. By 1958, he was employed as a milkman for Sealtest, a dairy company. His death certificate records his residence in Jacksonville at the time of his death.
Loyd died on January 17, 1958, at Duval Medical Center in Jacksonville, Florida. His death certificate identifies the cause as carcinoma of the lung with metastases. He was only 33 years old.

His funeral was held on January 19, 1958, at Airline Baptist Church near Mayo, Florida, with arrangements handled by Joe P. Burns Funeral Home. He was buried in the adjoining Airline Baptist Church Cemetery in Lafayette County, Florida.

Loyd's military gravestone commemorates his service during World War II with the inscription S1 USNR, identifying him as a Seaman First Class in the United States Naval Reserve. His obituary appeared in The Florida Times-Union on January 19, 1958.
Mary E. Singletary was born in South Carolina, probably in August 1842, according to the 1900 United States Federal Census. She was a daughter of Jacob and Eliza Singletary.
Mary first appears in the 1850 United States Federal Census in Sumter District, South Carolina, in the household of Jacob and Eliza B. Singletary. She was recorded as eight years old.
By 1860, Mary was living with the Singletary household in Decatur County, Georgia. The census recorded her as fourteen years old.
In 1870, Mary E. Singletary was enumerated in District 720 of Decatur County, Georgia, in the household of Jacob Singletary. Her age was recorded as twenty-three.

By 1880, Mary had moved to Lafayette County, Florida. She was enumerated in the household headed by Eliza Singletary, along with Sarah R., John V., and Jacob Singletary. Mary was recorded as twenty-two years old. Her reported age differs substantially from the ages recorded in earlier census records.

In 1900, Mary was living in Lafayette County, Florida, in the household of William and Sarah Johnson. She was identified as William's sister-in-law, while Eliza Singletary was identified as his mother-in-law. The census recorded Mary's birth as August 1842 and her marital status as single. These household relationships provide strong evidence that Mary and Sarah were sisters and that Eliza was their mother.
Mary's whereabouts after the 1900 census have not yet been established. No confirmed death record or burial location has been identified.

Sallie Sarah Singletary Spies was born on August 24, 1892, in Florida, the daughter of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary (1852–1931) and Ida Alla Miller Singletary (1873–1945). Her gravestone and Florida death certificate agree on her birth date. Although she appears as Sarah in early census records and Sallie in later records, her 1986 death certificate identifies her as Sallie Sarah Spies. Her obituary identifies her as a native of Lafayette County, Florida, where she spent much of her life.

Sallie grew up in Lafayette County, Florida, where her father worked as a farmer and was also identified as a minister. The 1900 United States Federal Census records her in her parents' household, with her birth listed as August 1892. Her siblings in the household included Eliza E., William Robert, Emma, and Henry Singletary.

Sallie continued living in Lafayette County during her childhood and early adulthood. She appears in her parents' household in the 1910 and 1920 federal censuses. The 1920 census records her as twenty-three years old, although her established birth date indicates that she was twenty-seven at the time. Such differences in reported ages occur elsewhere in the family's census records.

On May 2, 1920, Sallie Singletary married Horace W. Spies in Lafayette County, Florida. Their original marriage license was issued on May 1, 1920, by County Judge Hall W. Adams at the courthouse in Mayo. The marriage ceremony was performed the following day by J. J. Fannell, M.G., with J. R. Banks and Will Evans serving as witnesses. The marriage was filed and recorded on June 2, 1920, in Lafayette County Marriage License Record E, page 459.

The 1930 United States Federal Census appears to list Sallie in the household of her parents, Jacob and Ida Singletary, in the Day community of Lafayette County. She was recorded under the Singletary surname and apparently identified as single, despite her documented marriage to Horace Spies ten years earlier. The reason for this discrepancy has not been established. It is possible that the marriage had already ended or that the census information was recorded incorrectly, but neither explanation has been confirmed.

Following the death of her father on May 14, 1931, Sallie continued living in the Lafayette County community. The 1940 United States Federal Census records Sally Spies, age forty-seven, living in the household of her widowed mother, Ida Singletary. Her brothers Robert, Henry, and Giddy were also members of the household. Sallie was recorded as widowed, although her 1986 Florida death certificate later identified her marital status as divorced. The circumstances surrounding the end of her marriage to Horace W. Spies remain uncertain, and no divorce record or death record for Horace has yet been established.

Sallie remained connected to her siblings throughout her adult life. She was identified as a surviving sister in the February 1961 obituary of her brother William Robert Singletary. The obituary listed Mrs. Sally Spies of Lafayette County, Florida, along with her sisters Eliza Bell and Emma Evans and brothers Henry, Giddy, Jamie, and Jasper Singletary. This record confirms that she continued using the Spies surname more than forty years after her marriage.

In her later years, Sallie lived in Live Oak, Suwannee County, Florida. Her 1986 Florida death certificate records her usual residence as 1120 Helvenston in Live Oak and lists her occupation as homemaker. She was also a member of Bethel Creek Baptist Church, reflecting her continued association with the Lafayette County community where she had grown up and where several members of her family were buried.

Sallie died on Wednesday, May 21, 1986, at Suwannee County Hospital in Live Oak, Florida, following a long illness. She was ninety-three years old. Her Florida death certificate identifies her parents as Jacob Singletary and Ida Miller and records her marital status as divorced. The informant was Gid Singletary of Mayo, Florida.

Her obituary, published in The Florida Times-Union on May 23, 1986, identifies her as Sallie Singletary Spies, age ninety-three, of Live Oak. It describes her as a native of Lafayette County, a homemaker, and a member of Bethel Creek Baptist Church. The obituary identifies her surviving brother as Gid Singletary of Mayo, Florida. This provides additional evidence that Gid was the brother identified as Giddy or Giddie Singletary in earlier census records and in William Robert Singletary's 1961 obituary. Although the obituary names no other surviving siblings, their death dates must be established through separate records.

Funeral services were scheduled for 3:00 p.m. on May 23, 1986, at Bethel Creek Baptist Church, followed by burial in the church cemetery. Daniels Funeral Home of Live Oak was responsible for the arrangements. Sallie's gravestone at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery identifies her as Sallie Singletary Spies and records her birth on August 24, 1892, and death on May 21, 1986. These dates agree with her Florida death certificate.

Sarah R. Singletary was born in South Carolina around 1840. She was enumerated in the 1850 United States Federal Census in Sumter District, South Carolina, in the household of Jacob and Eliza B. Singletary. The census recorded her as ten years old.
By 1860, Sarah had moved with the Singletary household to Decatur County, Georgia. The federal census recorded her as nineteen years old.

In 1870, Sarah was enumerated in District 720 of Decatur County, Georgia, in the household of Jacob Singletary. The census recorded her name as Sarah A. Singletarry, age twenty-five, born in South Carolina. Earlier census records identified her as Sarah R. Singletary. The variation in her middle initial remains unresolved, although her 1890 marriage record later identified her as S. R. A. Singletary.

On January 30, 1890, Sarah married William Johnson in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license was issued on January 28, and the ceremony was performed by Elder J. A. Singletary, believed to be Sarah's brother, Reverend Jacob A. Singletary. The marriage was officially recorded on February 3, 1890. The original marriage record identifies the bride as Miss S. R. A. Singletary, providing additional evidence of her middle initials. Although she is identified as Sarah Ann Singletary in FamilySearch, her full middle names have not yet been independently established.

In 1900, Sarah was living in Lafayette County, Florida, with her husband, William Johnson. The federal census recorded her birth as March 1840 and her age as sixty. Her mother, Eliza Singletary, and sister, Mary Singletary, were also members of the household. Sarah was recorded as having given birth to no children, with none living. Interestingly, both Sarah and William were recorded as having been married for thirty years, suggesting a marriage around 1870. However, their original marriage record documents a ceremony on January 30, 1890. The reason for this discrepancy remains unresolved.

Sarah died on October 31, 1907, in Day, Lafayette County, Florida. Her death certificate records her birth year as 1840, identifies her husband as William Johnson, and gives her father's surname as Singletary. The certificate lists paralysis of the heart as the cause of death. Her husband, William Johnson, served as the informant, establishing that he was still living at the time of her death. The certificate records her burial location as Day, Florida, but does not identify a cemetery. Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery, where her mother Eliza Singletary is buried, is a possible burial location, although this has not been confirmed.

Silas P. Singletary was born in South Carolina, probably in March 1835. Both the 1900 United States Federal Census and a burial record report his birth as March 1835. However, federal census records from 1850, 1860, and 1870 consistently suggest a birth around 1839. His exact birth date has not been conclusively established.
In 1850, Silas was living in Sumter District, South Carolina, in the household of Jacob and Eliza B. Singletary. The federal census recorded him as eleven years old.

By 1860, Silas had moved with the Singletary household to Decatur County, Georgia. The census recorded him as twenty-one years old and born in South Carolina. The household included Jacob, Eliza, and several younger family members.

During the American Civil War, Silas P. Singletary served in the Confederate Army. The National Archives' Index to Compiled Service Records of Confederate Soldiers from Georgia (publication M226) identifies an S. P. Singletary as a private in Company A of the 59th Georgia Infantry. His exact dates of military service have not been established. A Confederate widow's pension application filed by Rachel Griffin Singletary in Thomas County, Georgia, in 1916 provides additional evidence connecting this soldier to her husband, Silas P. Singletary. The original compiled military service records have not yet been examined.

On October 14, 1869, Silas married Rachel Griffin in Decatur County, Georgia. The original county marriage register records the groom's name as Simon P. Singletary, indicating that he may also have been known by that name. The marriage was performed by J. W. Oliver, a minister of the gospel. Rachel's later Confederate widow's pension application also identifies her husband as S. P. Singletary and reports their marriage in October 1869.

In 1870, Silas remained in Decatur County, Georgia, where he was enumerated in the household of Jacob Singletary. He was recorded as thirty-one years old. Rachel Griffin, whom he had married the previous year, was also recorded in the household.

By June 1900, Silas was living in Thomas County, Georgia, with his wife Rachel and four children: Emma P., Mary, Robert, and Dollie. The census recorded his birth as March 1835, consistent with the information reported in his burial record.
Silas P. Singletary died on January 10, 1915, according to a burial record. He was buried at Springhill Christian Church Cemetery in Ochlocknee, Thomas County, Georgia.

Following Silas's death, his widow, Rachel Griffin Singletary, applied for a Confederate widow's pension in Thomas County, Georgia. The application, dated in 1916, identifies her husband as S. P. Singletary and provides information about their marriage and his military service. The application also contains a handwritten statement concerning differences in recollections of the couple's marriage. Their marriage date is independently documented in the original Decatur County marriage register dated October 14, 1869.
Viola Singletary was born around 1908 in Florida. She was the daughter of John V. Singletary and Mary Bryant Singletary.
The 1910 United States Federal Census lists Viola, approximately two years old, living with her parents and siblings in Lafayette County, Florida.

William Robert Singletary was born on May 3, 1894, in Florida, the son of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary (1852–1931) and Ida Alla Miller Singletary (1873–1945). He grew up in Lafayette County, Florida, where his family lived in the rural community around Day and Bethel Creek Baptist Church.

The 1900 United States Federal Census records William as Robert Singletary, living with his parents and siblings in Lafayette County. His birth was recorded as May 1894. The household included his sisters Eliza, Sarah, and Emma, and his brother Henry.

In the 1910 census, Robert was again living with his parents in Lafayette County. The household included several of his siblings, including Henry, Giddy, and Jamie. Census records from this period contain inconsistencies in the children's reported ages, which should be considered when evaluating their birth years.

On June 5, 1918, William registered for the World War I draft in Lafayette County, Florida. His registration identifies him as William Robert Singletary, living in Dowling Park, Florida, and employed by Jacob Singletary. He described himself as having brown eyes and brown hair. The registration records his birth date as May 3, 1897, three years later than the date recorded in the 1900 census, his death certificate, and his gravestone. The reason for this discrepancy is unknown.

The 1920 United States Federal Census records Robert, age 22, living with his parents in Lafayette County. In 1930, he was still living in the household of Jacob and Ida Singletary in the Day community. At that time, he was recorded as age 32 and employed as a laborer at a sawmill. These reported ages are consistent with a birth around 1897 or 1898 rather than 1894.

Following his father's death in May 1931, William continued living with his mother and several siblings. The 1940 census records Robert Singletary, age 45, in the household of his widowed mother, Ida, along with his brothers Henry and Giddy and his widowed sister Sally Spies. His reported age in 1940 is consistent with a birth in May 1894.
William's death certificate records that he was never married. No spouse or children have been identified in the records examined during this research.

William Robert Singletary died on February 22, 1961, at Suwannee County Hospital in Live Oak, Florida. His death certificate records his usual residence as Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. The immediate cause of death was recorded as probable acute myocardial failure, associated with coronary occlusion and hypertensive cardiovascular disease. He was sixty-six years old according to his recorded birth date.

His obituary reported that funeral services were held at Bethel Creek Baptist Church, with Reverend Tom Allen officiating. William was buried on February 24, 1961, at Bethel Creek Baptist Church Cemetery in Lafayette County, Florida.

William's obituary identified seven surviving siblings: sisters Eliza Bell, Sally Spies, and Emma Evans, and brothers Henry, Giddy, Jamie, and Jasper Singletary. This obituary provides important evidence for reconstructing the children of Reverend Jacob A. Singletary and Ida Alla Miller.

William's gravestone records his birth as May 3, 1894, and his death as February 22, 1961. These dates agree with his death certificate. Although his 1918 draft registration and some census records suggest a later birth year, May 3, 1894, is retained provisionally because it is supported by the 1900 census, his death certificate, and his gravestone.
Dicie Stewart married Albert Eugene Singletary on August 31, 1919, in Lafayette County, Florida, according to a Florida marriage record.

Albert's 1928 Florida death certificate identifies his wife with a name previously read as Daisy Stewart. The marriage record identifies her as Dicie Stewart. Further examination of the original records may help explain the discrepancy.
Additional information about Dicie's birth, parents, and later life has not yet been established.
Ann D., whose maiden name has not been established, was the wife of Heron Herrin. Family research identifies her as the mother of seven children born between approximately 1793 and 1810.
Following Heron's death in 1817, Ann reportedly married Levi J. Knight. According to family research, she later lived in Wayne County, Georgia, where she died around 1830.

Sarah Lusindy Wadsworth, also known as Sallie, was born March 19, 1840, according to her gravestone at Brady Cemetery in Florida. Her birthplace remains uncertain. The 1860 United States Census records her birthplace as Florida, while the 1880 census transcription identifies Georgia.
Sarah married Greenberry Blanton on December 6, 1857, in Madison County, Florida. Their marriage record identifies her as Sarah M. Wadsworth.
In the 1860 United States Census, Sarah and Greenberry were living in Lowndes County, Georgia, with two children, Emma E. Blanton and William T. Blanton.
Greenberry's whereabouts after 1860 remain uncertain. The published family history Aldermans in America reports that he died around 1863, but this date has not been independently verified.
Sarah subsequently married Everett Darling on March 28, 1879, in Madison County, Florida. Everett's surname also appears as Dowling in historical records.

In the 1880 United States Census, Sarah was living with Everett in Madison County, Florida. The household also included Liddy A. Blanton, age four, identified as Everett's stepdaughter. Liddy's biological father has not been established.

Sarah and Everett were the parents of Mary Frances Darling Mathis, born June 4, 1880, according to Mary's Florida death certificate. Mary's 1939 Social Security record gives her birth year as 1881, so the year remains subject to conflicting evidence.

Sarah's middle name is recorded inconsistently in surviving historical records. Her 1857 marriage record identifies her as Sarah M. Wadsworth. The 1880 census transcription identifies her as Sarah L. Dowling, while her gravestone identifies her as Sarah Lusindy Dowling. The reason for this discrepancy has not been established.
Sarah died March 30, 1908, according to her gravestone, and is buried at Brady Cemetery in Florida.
David Brewer Webb, known as Buddy, was born on June 22, 1941.
David was married to Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011). Florida divorce records document their divorce in Taylor County on June 6, 1975. Whether they subsequently remarried has not yet been established.
David died on February 6, 2007. He and Evelyn are commemorated on a shared gravestone at Waters Memorial Gardens in Steinhatchee, Taylor County, Florida.
The gravestone identifies four children: Stevie, Ricky, Connie Ray, and Debra. Their individual parentage has not yet been established.
David Steve Webb, known as Stevie, is the son of David Brewer Webb (1941–2007) and Evelyn Herrin (1934–2011).
Stevie grew up in the Taylor County, Florida, area and appears in a 1988 Taylor County High School yearbook index.
He is a maternal half-brother of Connie Ray Mathis and Richard (Ricky) Mathis.

military_service.notes: Hezekiah P. Williams is identified as a private in Company K of the 26th Georgia Infantry. His compiled military service record references six medical cards. His enlistment and discharge dates, as well as the circumstances of any medical treatment, have not yet been established. Source: National Archives, M226, Roll 65.

biograpy: Hezekiah Ponder Williams served as a private in Company K of the 26th Georgia Infantry during the American Civil War. His compiled Confederate military service record references six medical cards, although the circumstances of his military service and medical treatment have not yet been established.

On July 15, 1867, Hezekiah registered to vote in Clinch County, Georgia, during Reconstruction. His voter registration record includes an oath supporting the Constitution and laws of the United States.

biography: Isham Williams was born approximately 1823. He appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age 27. His relationship to the household head is not explicitly stated in the census.

John Williams was born approximately 1827. He appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age 23. His relationship to the household head is not explicitly stated in the census.
Laura Williams was born on April 29, 1855, in Homerville, Clinch County, Georgia.
She married Henry Palmer. She died on her 89th birthday on April 29, 1944, in Atkinson County, Georgia.

Martha Williams was born approximately 1835. She appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age 15. Her relationship to the household head is not explicitly stated in the census.

Mary Williams was born approximately 1834. She appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age 16. Her relationship to the household head is not explicitly stated in the census.
Mary Williams married Malachi M. Matthews on October 27, 1870, in Madison County, Florida.

The transcription of the Matthews family Bible records her death as July 16, 1903. Her birth year remains uncertain because the Bible transcription and the 1885 Florida Census provide conflicting information.

Sarah Williams was born approximately 1840. She appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age 10. Her relationship to the household head is not explicitly stated in the census.

military_service.notes: William M. Williams served as a private in Company K, 26th Georgia Infantry. He died on May 12, 1864, at Spotsylvania Courthouse, Virginia, during the Battle of Spotsylvania Court House. His older brother, Hezekiah Ponder Williams, also served in Company K of the 26th Georgia Infantry. William is buried in Spotsylvania Confederate Cemetery. A government headstone was requested in October 1929 and the application was verified in July 1930.

biography: William M. Williams was born in 1843 in Ware County, Georgia. He was the youngest son of John Williams and Nancy Smith Williams and a younger brother of Hezekiah Ponder Williams.
William appears in the 1850 United States Census in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia, at age seven.

During the American Civil War, William served as a private in Company K, 26th Georgia Infantry, Confederate Army. His older brother Hezekiah Ponder Williams also served in the same company and regiment.
William died on May 12, 1864, at Spotsylvania Courthouse, Virginia, during the Battle of Spotsylvania Court House. He was approximately 20 or 21 years old.

William was buried at Spotsylvania Confederate Cemetery in Virginia. In October 1929, Mrs. C. P. Andrews submitted an application to the War Department for a government headstone to mark his grave. The application was verified in July 1930.
Zilpha Williams was born around 1825 in Georgia, according to family research. She was a daughter of John Williams and Nancy Smith and a sister of Hezekiah Ponder Williams.

Zilpha married Joseph J. Cohen. In the 1850 United States Census, she appears as Zelpha Cohen, age 28, in the household of John and Nancy Williams in Ware County, Georgia. A five-year-old child named William Cohen was also recorded in the household.
Family research indicates that Zilpha died in 1905. Her exact birth and death dates have not yet been verified.

death_place: Suwannee River near Suwannee Springs, Florida
biography: Marie Richmond Evans was born around 1926 in Louisiana. Her parents and exact date of birth have not yet been established.

By April 1950, Marie was married to Frederick (Fred) Evans, son of Willie Evans and Emma Singletary Evans. The couple lived in Suwannee County, Florida. The 1950 United States federal census recorded Marie, age 24, with Fred and four children: Charles Richmond, age 10; Donald Richmond, age 8; Freddie Evans, age 2; and Willie Evans, age 1. Charles and Donald were identified as Fred's stepsons. It is not yet known whether Richmond was Marie's maiden name or a surname from an earlier marriage.

On June 7, 1952, Marie and her family were enjoying an outing along the Suwannee River near Suwannee Springs, Florida. According to contemporary newspaper reports, Donald Ray entered the water and was caught in a strong undertow. His older brother Charles attempted to rescue him, followed by Marie. All three drowned. Fred also entered the river in an attempt to save his family and was rescued by his brother-in-law, Owen Lassiter.

The tragedy was reported in newspapers, including The St. Augustine Record on June 8, 1952. Marie was approximately 26 years old at the time of her death. Her burial location has not yet been established.

military_service.notes: Fred Evans entered the United States Army as a private during World War II. His enlistment record lists March 11, 1943, at Camp Blanding, Florida, while a separate military service index lists March 18, 1943. His military gravestone identifies his rank as Technician Fifth Grade (TEC 5). His military unit, assignments, and overseas service, if any, have not yet been established.

biography: Fred Evans Sr. was born on May 21, 1924, in Dowling Park, Suwannee County, Florida, the son of Willie Evans and Emma Singletary Evans. His maternal grandparents were Reverend Jacob A. Singletary and Ida Alla Miller Singletary. His birth date is supported by his gravestone and Social Security records, although his 1942 draft registration records May 3, 1924, and a military service index records May 1, 1924.

The 1940 United States federal census recorded Fred, age 16, living with his parents in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. Also in the household were his older brother Ernest Evans, his sister Gracie Lassiter, and his brother-in-law Owen Lassiter.

On June 30, 1942, shortly after his eighteenth birthday, Fred registered for the World War II draft in Live Oak, Suwannee County, Florida. His registration card listed his residence as General Delivery, Live Oak, and identified his mother, Mrs. Emma Evans, as the person who would always know his address. He was employed by Dan Sanders, with his place of employment listed as Madison Highway in Live Oak. The card described him as five feet nine and one-half inches tall, weighing 135 pounds, with blue eyes, blond hair, and a light complexion.

During World War II, Fred served in the United States Army. His Army enlistment record indicates that he enlisted on March 11, 1943, at Camp Blanding, Florida. At the time, he was single without dependents, had a grammar school education, and his civilian occupation was classified as a semiskilled chauffeur or driver. He entered military service as a private and was later identified as a Technician Fifth Grade (TEC 5), according to his military gravestone. A separate military service index lists an enlistment date of March 18, 1943, and a discharge date of January 18, 1946. His specific unit, assignments, and locations of military service have not yet been established.

The 1945 Florida State Population Census recorded Fred, age 21, in the household of his parents, Willie and Emma Evans, in Precinct 1, Live Oak, Suwannee County, Florida. Other household members included his brother Ernest, Elizabeth Evans, his sister Grace Lassiter, her husband Owen Lassiter, and their young son Owen Jr. Elizabeth may have been Ernest's wife, although that relationship has not yet been confirmed. Because Fred was serving in the Army during this period, his enumeration does not necessarily establish that he was physically present in the household when the census was taken.

By April 1950, Fred was married to Marie Richmond Evans. The couple lived in Suwannee County, Florida, with four children: Charles Richmond, age 10; Donald Richmond, age 8; Freddie Evans, age 2; and Willie Evans, age 1. The 1950 federal census identified Charles and Donald as Fred's stepsons. Their biological father has not yet been identified, and it is not known whether Richmond was Marie's maiden name or a surname from an earlier marriage.

On June 7, 1952, Fred and his family were enjoying an outing along the Suwannee River near Suwannee Springs, Florida. According to contemporary newspaper reports, Donald Ray entered the river and was caught in a powerful undertow. His older brother Charles attempted to rescue him, followed by their mother Marie. All three drowned. Fred also entered the river in an attempt to save his family and was swept into the current. His brother-in-law, Owen Lassiter, managed to rescue Fred, although he was unable to save Marie and the two boys. The newspaper reports identified the boys as Charles and Donald Ray Evans, while the 1950 census recorded their surname as Richmond.

Fred survived the tragedy and continued living in Florida. He was identified as a surviving son residing in Jacksonville in the 1971 obituary of his father, Willie Evans, and again in the 1984 obituary of his mother, Emma Singletary Evans.

Fred Evans Sr. died on July 26, 1993, at the age of 69. He was buried in Live Oak Cemetery in Live Oak, Suwannee County, Florida. His military gravestone commemorates his World War II service in the United States Army and identifies his rank as Technician Fifth Grade. His exact place of death has not yet been established.

Hope Wayland Sullivan was born on September 12, 1920, in Mayo, Lafayette County, Florida. He was the son of John M. Sullivan and Arzada Boyd Sullivan, as identified on his gravestone. His World War II draft registration also identifies John M. Sullivan as his employer and the person who would always know his address in February 1942.

On February 15, 1942, Hope registered for the World War II draft in Mayo, Florida. He was 21 years old and lived on Route 2 in Mayo. His registration card identified John M. Sullivan as both his employer and the person who would always know his address. The card described Hope as five feet eight inches tall, weighing 118 pounds, with blue eyes, brown hair, and a ruddy complexion. His registration does not, by itself, establish military service.

On April 17, 1942, Hope married Ida Mae Herrin in Lafayette County, Florida. Their marriage license was issued that day in Mayo, and the certificate records that they were married at a private home. The marriage was recorded on April 18, 1942.

Hope and Ida Mae had a family that included several children with the Sullivan surname. Hope's obituary identifies seven surviving children: Nell Slaughter, Connie Mack Sullivan, Billy John Sullivan, Wayland Sullivan, Paul (Mike) Sullivan, Drew Sullivan, and Jack Sullivan. Ida Mae's later gravestone also names Stella S. Osborn, whose relationship to Hope has not yet been independently established.

Hope later lived in Perry, Taylor County, Florida, where he worked as a lineman for an electrical company. According to his obituary, he had lived in Perry for approximately five years before his death.

Hope died on May 27, 1982, in Taylor County, Florida, at the age of 61. At the time of his death, he was living in Perry and working as a lineman for an electrical company. His funeral was held at Airline Baptist Church in Mayo, Florida, with burial in the church cemetery. His gravestones commemorate his life, identify his parents as John M. and Arzada Boyd Sullivan, and include the inscription 'Daddy' and 'Gone But Not Forgotten.'

His military gravestone identifies his rank as Seaman Second Class (S2). His ship assignments and locations of service have not yet been established.

biography: Lawrence Monroe Secreast was born on February 18, 1912, in Lenoir, Caldwell County, North Carolina. A North Carolina delayed birth certificate index identifies his parents as Daniel R. Secreast and Stella Wilson. His first name appears as Laurence in some birth records and his surname appears as Secrest in certain marriage and divorce records.

The 1920 United States census recorded Lawrence as a child in Lower Creek Township, Caldwell County, North Carolina, in the household of Daniel R. Secreast. The household also included a woman recorded as Flossie. Her relationship to Lawrence's birth mother, Stella Wilson, has not yet been established.

On September 30, 1933, Lawrence married Ruth A. Sherrill in Buncombe County, North Carolina. Both were recorded as 21 years old. On October 16, 1940, Lawrence registered for the World War II draft while residing in Granite Falls, Caldwell County, North Carolina. His registration identified Mrs. Ruth A. Secreast as his wife. He was employed by Barger-Ashe Roofing Company in Lenoir.

During World War II, Lawrence served in the United States Navy. A military service index records his enlistment on March 22, 1944, and discharge on December 23, 1945. His military gravestone identifies his rank as Seaman Second Class (S2). His ship assignments and locations of service have not yet been established.
Lawrence and Ruth divorced on November 22, 1946, in St. Johns County, Florida, according to a Florida divorce record.

Lawrence subsequently married Margaret Fussell, who was born on November 4, 1913, in Georgia. They had a daughter, Stella Emily Secreast, born on January 13, 1948, in Macon, Georgia. The dates of Lawrence and Margaret's marriage and its ending have not yet been established.

On April 26, 1950, the United States federal census recorded Lawrence, age 38, living in Pensacola, Escambia County, Florida, with Margaret, age 36, and their daughter Stella, age 2. Lawrence worked as a cabinet maker in a furniture shop.

On April 5, 1959, Lawrence married Ida Mae Herrin Sullivan, known as Shorty. Their marriage was recorded in Wakulla County, Florida, and the exact date appears on their shared gravestone. Ida Mae had previously been married to Hope Wayland Sullivan and had children from that marriage. Lawrence's daughter Stella became part of this blended family.

Lawrence worked in the roofing trade and was described as a retired roofer in his obituary. Earlier records identify him as an employee of Barger-Ashe Roofing Company in Lenoir, North Carolina, in 1940, and as a cabinet maker working in a furniture shop in Pensacola, Florida, in 1950. He was a member of Granite Falls Methodist Church in Granite Falls, North Carolina.

Lawrence died at his home in Fanning Springs, Florida, on June 3, 1982, following a long illness. His obituary, published in the Tallahassee Democrat on June 5, 1982, identified his surviving wife Ida Mae, daughter Stella Osborn, members of the Sullivan family, brothers Arno, Bob, and Cade Secreast, and 25 grandchildren. Funeral services were scheduled at Joe P. Burns Funeral Home Chapel in Perry, Florida. The obituary announced burial at Spring Warrior Cemetery in Taylor County, although other family records identify Old Town Memorial Cemetery as his burial location.

Stella Emily Secreast was born on January 13, 1948, in Macon, Bibb County, Georgia. She was the daughter of Lawrence Monroe Secreast and Margaret Fussell Secreast. Her maternal grandparents were Dr. Thomas Daniel Fussell and Sarah Redman Fussell.
The 1950 United States federal census recorded Stella, age two, living with her parents in Pensacola, Escambia County, Florida. Her father worked as a cabinet maker in a furniture shop.

Following her father's marriage to Ida Mae Herrin Sullivan on April 5, 1959, Stella became part of the extended Sullivan-Secreast family. Her stepbrothers included Michael Paul Sullivan and Billy John Sullivan. A family photograph also shows Stella alongside Ida Mae and several members of the Sullivan family.

Stella attended Savannah Technical College, where she earned an associate degree in Forest Technology. She subsequently worked at Fort Stewart, Georgia, as a forest technician and endangered species technician. During her career, she identified rare and endangered plant species at Fort Stewart and in the surrounding area.
Stella was a member of Ellabell Methodist Church and the Horticultural Society. She enjoyed botany, growing orchids, flowers and vegetables, as well as fishing and hunting.

Stella married Steve Osborn. Her obituary described Steve as her husband of 38 years at the time of her death. Her children included Ernest Coren Rahn, Donald Lee Rahn, and Sarah Emily Osborn. The dates and circumstances of any earlier marriage have not yet been established.

Stella died on February 19, 2020, at St. Joseph's Hospital, at the age of 72. Her obituary identified her husband Steve, her three children, five grandchildren, and her stepbrothers Mike Sullivan and Billy John Sullivan among her surviving family. She was preceded in death by her granddaughter Krista Breanna Rahn.
Funeral services were held on February 22, 2020, at Ellabell Methodist Church in Georgia, with burial at Bethany Campground Cemetery.

Margaret Fussell was born on November 4, 1913, in Georgia. She was the daughter of Dr. Thomas Daniel Fussell and Sarah Redman Fussell, as identified in the obituary of her daughter, Stella Emily Secreast Osborn.

Margaret married Lawrence Monroe Secreast, who was born on February 18, 1912, in Lenoir, North Carolina. Lawrence had previously been married to Ruth A. Sherrill, whom he divorced on November 22, 1946, in St. Johns County, Florida. The exact date and location of Margaret and Lawrence's marriage have not yet been established.
Margaret and Lawrence had a daughter, Stella Emily Secreast, born on January 13, 1948, in Macon, Bibb County, Georgia.

On April 26, 1950, the United States federal census recorded Margaret, age 36, living with her husband Lawrence, age 38, and their daughter Stella, age two, in Pensacola, Escambia County, Florida. Lawrence was employed as a cabinet maker in a furniture shop. The census recorded Margaret and Stella as having been born in Georgia.

Margaret and Lawrence's marriage ended sometime before Lawrence married Ida Mae Herrin Sullivan on April 5, 1959. The date and circumstances of the end of Margaret and Lawrence's marriage have not yet been established.
Margaret died on January 26, 1984, at the age of 70. She was buried at Sharon Baptist Church Cemetery in Telfair County, Georgia.

David Sears was born in North Carolina in 1791, the son of John Sears, a Revolutionary War soldier. According to Pioneers of Wiregrass Georgia, his father moved the family to Montgomery County, Georgia, around 1795 or 1796.
David married Levicy Nobles on April 19, 1810, in Montgomery County, Georgia. Levicy was the daughter of Lewis Sanders Nobles, who also served during the Revolutionary War.

David and Levicy raised thirteen children, including Charity Sears (1812–1898), who married Levi Herrin. Through Charity, they became ancestors of both branches of the Herrin family featured in the story Two Branches of the Herrin Family Reunite.

On June 20, 1809, David was commissioned an ensign in the 52nd District of Emanuel County. During the War of 1812, he served as a private in Captain John G. Colbert's company, 2nd Regiment of Georgia Militia. He enlisted on October 12, 1814, and was discharged on March 15, 1815, according to the published family history.

Around 1825, David moved his family from Montgomery County to what was then Ware County, Georgia, settling in the 586th Georgia Militia District. This territory subsequently became part of Clinch, Coffee, and Atkinson counties.
The published family history references David in the 1820 Montgomery County census, the 1830, 1840, and 1850 Ware County censuses, and the 1860 Coffee County census.
David died in 1879. He and Levicy were buried at Union Hill Congregational Church cemetery, where they were members.

Levicy Nobles was born in Georgia in 1792, the daughter of Lewis Sanders Nobles, who is identified as a Revolutionary War soldier in Pioneers of Wiregrass Georgia. The name of her mother has not yet been established in the records collected for this archive.

On April 19, 1810, Levicy married David Sears (1791–1879) in Montgomery County, Georgia. Their marriage is documented in a historical marriage record and is also recorded in Pioneers of Wiregrass Georgia.

Levicy and David raised thirteen children: Luraney, Charity, Hiram, Lavina, Harriet, Matilda, George W., Charlotte, Mary, Tobitha, Benjamin Franklin, Thaddeus, and David. Their children were born between approximately 1811 and 1830.

Among their children was Charity Sears (1812–1898), who married Levi Herrin (1804–1890). Through Charity, Levicy became an ancestor of both branches of the Herrin family that eventually reunited through the marriage of William Levi Herrin and Laura Etta Palmer in April 1916.

Around 1825, the Sears family moved from Montgomery County to what was then Ware County, Georgia, settling in the 586th Georgia Militia District. The area later became part of Clinch, Coffee, and Atkinson counties as county boundaries changed.
Levicy lived through a period of considerable change in southern Georgia, including the years leading up to the American Civil War. She died in 1868, three years after the war ended.
Levicy and David were members of Union Hill Congregational Church and were buried in its cemetery near present-day Axson, Atkinson County, Georgia.
